trust_boundaries: edge-to-prod: ingress_controller to frontend_pods (internal cluster routing)
namespace-prod-to-data: backend_pods via service_mesh to database/cache namespace
namespace-isolation: prod and data namespaces separated by NetworkPolicy
architecture_summary.operational_context: Kubernetes cluster running multi-namespace production workload with service mesh

threat_actors.name: External Attacker
threat_actors.motivation: Workload compromise to access container runtime or data within the cluster
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Exploitation of internet-facing service via ingress controller or vulnerable frontend pod
non_capabilities: No Kubernetes API server direct access from internet

threat_actors.name: Compromised Container Workload
threat_actors.motivation: Lateral movement from one compromised pod to cluster-level access
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Container breakout from application vulnerability or misconfigured security context
non_capabilities: No node-level credentials without explicit service account binding
No cross-namespace access without NetworkPolicy bypass
No etcd direct access without API server credentials

attack_paths.entry_point: Internet-facing HTTPS port with CVE in Nginx ingress controller
attack_paths.impact: Remote code execution in ingress namespace, potential cluster RBAC token access
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Ingress controller CVEs are routinely published; version lag on patch management is common

attack_paths.entry_point: Remote code execution in frontend application via injected payload
attack_paths.impact: Shell access within frontend pod, access to service account token and cluster DNS
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Frontend applications commonly have deserialization or injection vulnerabilities; pod exec gives k8s SA token

attack_paths.entry_point: Privileged service account token from AP-002 used to create new pod in prod namespace
attack_paths.impact: Malicious pod deployed with host path mounts or privileged context, enabling node escape
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Overly broad RBAC is pervasive in k8s; pods/create permission combined with host mounts enables node escape

attack_paths.entry_point: Database credentials in Kubernetes Secrets without encryption at rest
attack_paths.impact: Database credentials exfiltrated from unencrypted etcd or environment variable leak
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Kubernetes Secrets are base64 — not encrypted — by default unless etcd encryption is configured; commonly overlooked

attack_paths.entry_point: Service mesh control plane API accessible from compromised pod without mTLS policy enforcement
attack_paths.impact: Cluster topology enumeration and inter-service traffic interception if mTLS not enforced
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Service mesh mTLS often deployed in permissive mode during migration; PERMISSIVE mode allows cleartext

attack_paths.entry_point: Database credentials from AP-004 used for direct database connection from pod
attack_paths.impact: Full database read/write access bypassing application-layer controls
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Once credentials obtained from Secrets, direct DB connection via pod exec or kubectl port-forward is trivial

attack_paths.entry_point: Redis cache accessible within data namespace without auth from backend pod
attack_paths.impact: Cache poisoning or session token theft affecting all authenticated users
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Redis in Kubernetes commonly deployed without requirepass; namespace isolation often insufficient without NetworkPolicy

attack_paths.entry_point: Disabling mTLS policy for targeted service via control plane API access
attack_paths.impact: Cleartext inter-service traffic exposes session data and API tokens within the mesh
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Service mesh control plane access requires elevated RBAC; achievable after AP-003 but adds attack steps

mitigations.control_name: Ingress controller version pinning and automated CVE scanning
Pod security admission with non-root enforcement
RBAC least privilege — deny pods/create to application service accounts
etcd encryption at rest for Secrets
Service mesh mTLS STRICT mode enforcement

findings.severity_rationale: Unencrypted etcd Secrets allow any user with etcd read access to obtain all credentials; default Kubernetes configuration
RBAC misconfiguration allowing pods/create with host mounts enables node escape from compromised pod
Database credentials obtained from Secrets enable direct full-access DB connection bypassing all app controls
Service mesh in permissive mode allows cleartext intra-cluster traffic; mTLS migration required
Redis without authentication enables cache poisoning affecting all sessions in the cache namespace
Ingress CVE risk is partially mitigated by scanning; residual depends on patch cadence
